It shall be unlawful for any person to possess, offer for sale, sell, use, or explode any fireworks without a permit issued from the village. Fireworks shall mean any item as defined in the Fireworks Use Act, 425 ILCS 35/0.01 et seq., and includes, but is not limited to, blank cartridges, toy cannons, firecrackers, torpedoes, skyrockets, bottle rockets, Roman candles, bombs, or like devices containing any explosive substance.

It shall be unlawful to build, light or permit to burn any bonfire so close to any building or structure as to endanger such structure or on any public street or sidewalk pavement or at any time between sunset and 6:00 a.m.

There is hereby adopted by reference that publication known as the Fire Prevention Code, 1976 edition, and the November, 1982, amendments, recommended by the American Insurance Association. Three copies of such publication are on file in the office of the village clerk and are available for public use, inspection and examination.

In addition, there is hereby adopted by reference that publication known as BOCA National Fire Prevention Code, 1999 edition, by the Building Officials Code Administrators International, Inc. Three copies of such publication are on file in the office of the village clerk and are available for public use, inspection and examination.
In the event of any conflict between the two codes adopted by this section, that code which is more strict shall apply.
Wherever the term "municipality" is used in the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code, it shall be held to mean the village.
Wherever the term "corporation counsel" is used in the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code, it shall be held to mean the attorney for the village.
The fire prevention codes shall be enforced by the fire department.
The chief of the fire department is permitted to detail such members of the fire department as inspectors as shall from time to time be necessary.

A report of the fire department shall be made annually and transmitted to the board of trustees. It shall contain all proceedings under the fire prevention codes, with such statistics as the fire chief decides to include therein. The chief shall also recommend any amendments to the fire prevention codes which, in his judgment, shall be desirable.
The chief may request and shall receive so far as may be necessary, in the discharge of his duties, the assistance and cooperation of other officials of the village.

Right of entry. Whenever it is necessary to make an inspection to enforce the provision of the village codes, or whenever the fire inspector has reasonable cause to believe that there exists in a building or upon any premises any condition or violations of village code which make the building or premises unsafe, dangerous or hazardous, the fire inspector shall have the authority to enter the building or premises unsafe, dangerous or hazardous; the fire inspector shall also have the authority to enter the building or premises at all reasonable times to inspect or to perform the duties imposed upon the fire inspector by this Code. If such building or premises is occupied, the fire inspector shall present credentials to the occupant and request entry. If such building or premises is unoccupied, the fire inspector shall first make a reasonable effort to locate the owner or other person having charge of control of the building or premises and request entry. If entry is refused, the fire inspector has recourse to every remedy provided by law to secure entry.
Establishment of limits of districts in which storage of explosives and blasting agents is to be prohibited

The limits referred to in section 12.5b of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code, in which storage of explosives and blasting agents is prohibited, are hereby established as follows: The entire village.
Establishment of limits of districts in which manufacture and storage of fireworks is to be prohibited

The limits referred to in section 13.3a of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code, in which manufacture and storage of fireworks is prohibited, are hereby established as follows: The entire village.
Establishment of limits of districts in which storage of flammable liquids in outside aboveground tanks is to be prohibited — clause a

The limits referred to in section 16.22a of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code in which storage of flammable liquids in outside aboveground tanks is prohibited, are hereby established as follows: All property which is not zoned "I."
Establishment of limits of districts in which storage of flammable liquids in outside aboveground tanks is to be prohibited — clause b

The limits referred to in section 16.61 of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code, in which new bulk plants or terminals for flammable or combustible liquids are prohibited, are hereby established as follows: All property which is not zoned "I."
Establishment of limits in which bulk storage of liquefied petroleum gases is to be restricted

The limits referred to in section 21.6a of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code, in which bulk storage of liquefied petroleum gas is restricted, are hereby established as follows: All property which is not zoned "I."
Establishment of motor vehicle routes for vehicles transporting explosives and blasting agents

The routes referred to in section 12.7o of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code for vehicles transporting explosives and blasting agents are hereby established as follows: Harlam Avenue and 39th Street.
Establishment of motor vehicle routes for vehicles transporting hazardous chemicals or other dangerous articles

The routes referred to in section 20.14 of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code for vehicles transporting hazardous chemicals and other dangerous articles are hereby established as follows: Harlam Avenue and 39th Street.
Establishment of fire lanes on private property devoted to public use
The fire lanes referred to in section 28.16 of the American Insurance Association's Fire Prevention Code are as established by ordinance.

The fire chief shall have power to modify any of the provisions of the Fire Prevention Code upon application in writing by the owner or lessee, or his duly authorized agent, when there are practical difficulties in the way of carrying out the strict letter of the code, provided that the intent of the code shall be, observed, public safety secured, and substantial justice done. The particulars of such modification when granted or allowed and the decision of the chief thereon shall be entered upon the records of the department, and a signed copy shall be furnished to the applicant.

Whenever the fire chief shall disapprove an application or refuse to grant a permit applied for, or when it is claimed that the provisions of the code do not apply or that the true intent and meaning of the code have been misconstrued or wrongly interpreted, the applicant is permitted to appeal from the decision of the chief to the board of trustees within 30 days from the date of decision appealed.
New materials, processes or occupancies which require permits — clause a

The building official, the fire chief and the village president shall act as a committee to determine and specify, after giving affected persons an opportunity to be heard, any new materials, processes or occupancies, which shall require permits, in addition to those now enumerated in the Fire Prevention Code.
New materials, processes or occupancies which require permits — clause b
The chief shall post such list in a conspicuous place in his office and distribute copies thereof to interested persons.

Any person who shall violate any of the provisions of the Fire Prevention Code or fail to comply therewith, or who shall violate or fail to comply with any order made under such code, or who shall build in violation of any detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved under such code, or any certificate or permit issued under such code, and from which no appeal has been taken, or who shall fail to comply with such an order as affirmed or modified by the board of trustees or by a court of competent jurisdiction, within the time fixed in this section, shall severally for each and every such violation and noncompliance, respectively, be guilty of an offense. The imposition of one penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation or permit it to continue, and all such persons shall be required to correct or remedy such violations or defects within a reasonable time. When not otherwise specified, each ten days that prohibited conditions are maintained shall constitute a separate offense.
The application of the penalty in subsection (a) of this section shall not be held to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions.
Where required. All buildings of residential or mixed occupancy having any residential units shall be equipped with approved operable smoke detectors in a manner prescribed in this article.

Location. Not less than one approved smoke detector shall be installed in each single-family residential unit and multiple dwelling unit as defined in the comprehensive zoning ordinance of the village. A detector shall be installed on the ceiling and at least six inches from any wall or on a wall located from six to 12 inches from the ceiling and within 15 feet of all rooms used for sleeping purposes, with not less than one detector per living level.

Stairwell installation. All multiple dwellings and buildings of mixed occupancy having any residential units shall contain not less than one approved smoke detector at the uppermost ceiling of all interior stairwells. All approved smoke detectors required in this section shall be installed on the ceiling at least six inches from the wall or on a wall located from six to 12 inches from the ceiling.

Standards. All approved smoke detectors required in this section shall be either an ionization chamber or photoelectric type and shall comply with all the specifications of the Underwriters' Laboratories, Inc., (UL), Standard UL 217 (Standard for Safety-Single and Multiple Station Smoke Detectors 1976) and any applicable provisions of the electrical code adopted pursuant to article IV, chapter 18 of this Code.
Exceptions. The provisions of this article shall not be applicable in buildings which contain an approved automatic sprinkler system throughout.
Installation, maintenance and location of fire detectors in mixed occupancy buildings

All mixed occupancy buildings shall be equipped with fire detectors located in the business and storage sections of such buildings in addition to the smoke detectors installed in the dwelling units. Such fire detectors shall be approved by the Underwriters' Laboratories, Inc., (UL) and shall be installed and maintained pursuant to the requirements of the National Fire Protection Code, 1978 edition. The alarm system from the fire detectors shall be directly connected to the village fire department.
Smoke detectors and fire detectors; unlawful to render inoperable

It shall be unlawful for any person to remove batteries from any smoke detector or in any way make inoperable any smoke detector or fire detector as provided for in this article, except that these provisions shall not apply to any building owner, manager or agent in the normal procedure of replacing batteries.

Kerosene contained in the fuel tanks of motor vehicles, engines or like machines, or fuel oil burners, when such tanks are permanently connected with the motor engines, machines or burners which they supply and for the purpose of supplying the same; or
Petroleum or fuel oil kept and stored for use in fuel oil burners used by persons on the premises.
Adoption of N.F.P.A. 704 System of Hazard Identification

All aboveground storage tanks in the village shall be identified with the National Fire Protection Association (N.F.P.A.) 704 System of Hazard Identification. The latest edition of the N.F.P.A. 704 System of Hazard Identification is adopted by reference as if fully set forth in this section.

No person shall manufacture, refine, blend, compound, keep, store, sell, distribute or use or permit the manufacturing, refining, blending, compounding, keeping, storing, selling, distributing or using within the village of any naphtha, gasoline, benzine, kerosene, petroleum, fuel oil, or other highly volatile oils, alcohol and flammable liquids without first having obtained a license therefor in the manner provided in this article.

Required. No person shall install, construct or erect any refinery, filling station, storage tank or container within the village for gasoline, benzine, naphtha, other highly volatile oils, alcohol and flammable liquids of larger capacity than five gallons or for kerosene or petroleum or fuel oil of larger capacity than 50 gallons, without first having obtained a permit so to do in the manner provided in this section.

Application, issuance and revocation. A person desiring to obtain the permit required by the provisions of this article shall make written application to the board of trustees; such application shall be filed with the village clerk and shall state the place where the same is to be installed, constructed or erected, the number, character and capacity thereof and the purpose of the same and shall be accompanied by a detailed specification of the manner of construction, installation and erection and the location of the filling station, refinery, storage tank or container in which such naphtha, gasoline, benzine, kerosene, fuel oil, petroleum, other volatile oils, alcohol and flammable liquids is to be manufactured, refined, blended, compounded, stored, contained or supplied, together with pumps or other equipment used in connection therewith, and a blueprint of the plans therefor, or a correct diagram of such plans, which plans, specifications, and blueprints and diagrams must bear the approval of the village president. Upon the granting of the application by the board of trustees, a permit for such installation, construction or erection shall be issued by the village clerk of the party applying therefor upon the payment to the village clerk, in advance, of the required fee; provided, however, such permit shall not waive or affect the obligation of any person to pay the annual license fee. The issuance of permits to install or alter any tank or container beneath any boulevard shall be discretionary with the board of trustees and any such permit when issued may be revoked at any time by the board of trustees if deemed for the best interest of the village and for the protection and convenience of the public.

Pursuant to Article VII, Section 6 of the Illinois Constitution, and 65 ILCS 5/1-2-1, the following ordinance is promulgated in order to regulate the inspection, testing, maintenance, correction, and repair of fire hydrants located on private property in the Village of Stickney and those fire hydrants located in the rights-of-way of public highways of the Village of Stickney that the village does not own.
Adoption of National Fire Protection Association Publication 25

All private fire hydrants must conform to the NFPA Standard, as defined in section 34-202, above. The National Fire Protection Association's Publication 25 is hereby adopted by reference as if set forth fully herein. Three copies shall be on file with the village clerk and are available for public use, inspection, and examination.

Responsibility for properly maintaining a private fire hydrant shall be that of the owner of the property or the owner's designee. Where the owner of a private fire hydrant has designated an occupant, management firm, or managing individual, through specific provisions in the lease, written use agreement, or management contract, to be responsible for the inspection, testing and maintenance of a private fire hydrant in accordance with this article, the owner's designee shall comply with the requirements of this article and shall be subject to enforcement of this article in the event of a failure to so comply.

By means of periodic inspections, tests, maintenance, correction, and repair as set forth in section 34-205, below, every private fire hydrant shall be maintained in proper working condition, consistent with this article, the NFPA Standard, and the manufacturer's specifications or recommendations. In the event of a conflict between or among any of the foregoing, the strictest regulation shall apply.

Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair shall be implemented with the procedures meeting or exceeding those established in this article and the NFPA Standard, and shall be in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications or recommendations. In the event of a conflict between or among any of the foregoing, the strictest regulation shall apply. Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction, and repair shall be performed by qualified maintenance personnel or a qualified contractor.

The owner or owner's designee shall notify the fire department before testing or shutting down a private fire hydrant or its water supply. This notification shall include the purpose for the shutdown, the private fire hydrant involved, and the estimated time that the hydrant will be impaired. Notice shall be effective if given in writing and provided to the fire department no less than 48 hours prior to such shutting-down.
The owner or owner's designee shall notify the fire department when the private fire hydrant is returned to service. Such notice may be given in writing or orally to the fire department.

The owner or owner's designee shall correct or repair any deficiencies, damaged parts, or impairments found while performing the inspection, testing, and maintenance requirements of this article, in the time frames set forth in section 34-205, below.

The owner or owner's designee shall correct or repair any deficiencies, damaged parts, or impairments of any private fire hydrant of which the owner or owner's designee has knowledge or, in the exercise of reasonable care, ought to have knowledge.
Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair — clause 1

On or before October 1 of each year, the owner or the owner's designee shall inspect, test, maintain, and if necessary, correct, and repair each private fire hydrant to ensure proper functioning, with the necessary repair or corrective action taken as shown in the table inset below.
Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair — clause 2

The owner or owner's designee shall conduct an inspection of a private fire hydrant after each time the hydrant is operated, and shall correct or repair any deficiencies within five business days of finding the same. If it is not commercially feasible for the owner to make such repairs within five business days of finding a deficiency, the owner or owner's designee shall notify the fire department immediately, both orally and in writing, of the defect and the reason that the defect cannot be repaired within five business days. Where a deficiency cannot reasonably be repaired within five business days, the owner or owner's designee shall correct or repair any deficiencies within a reasonable amount of time.
Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair — clause 3

When conducting a test of a private fire hydrant, the hydrant shall be opened fully and water flowed until all foreign material has cleared.

a.

Flow shall be maintained for not less than one minute.

b.

After operation, the hydrant shall be observed for proper drainage from the barrel.

c.

Full drainage shall take no longer than 60 minutes.

d.

Where soil conditions or other factors are such that the hydrant barrel does not drain within 60 minutes, or where the ground water level is above that of the hydrant drain, the water in the barrel shall be pumped out.

e.

A hydrant that does not drain as required shall be identified clearly as needing pumping after each operation. This shall be accomplished by affixing a tag, designated by the fired department for hydrants in need of pumping, to the hydrant.
Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair — clause 4
Private fire hydrants shall be lubricated annually to ensure that all stems, caps, plugs, and threads are in proper operating condition.
Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair — clause 5
Private fire hydrants shall be kept free of snow, ice, or other materials and protected against mechanical damage so that free access is ensured.
Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair — clause 6

The owner or the owner's designee has a continuing duty to ensure that the private fire hydrant is in proper working condition pursuant to the requirements of this article, and shall repair a private fire hydrant which is impaired or otherwise does not function as required by this article, the NFPA Standard, or the manufacturer's specifications within the applicable time frame set forth in this section.
Inspection, testing, maintenance, correction and repair — clause 7

After completing all necessary repairs to a private fire hydrant, the owner or the owner's designee shall inspect and test the hydrant as necessary consistent with the standards of this article, including without limitation Table 1, to ensure that the hydrant is operational.

Referenced Table 1 from section 34-205:
Condition	Corrective Action
Inaccessible	Make accessible
Barrel contains water or ice (presence could indicate a faulty drain or a leaky hydrant valve)	Repair and drain
Improper drainage from barrel	Repair drain
Leaks at outlets or at top of hydrant	Repair or replace gaskets, packing, or parts as necessary
Cracks in hydrant barrel	Repair or replace
Tightness of outlets	Lubricate if necessary, tighten if necessary
Worn, damaged nozzle threads	Repair or replace
Worn hydrant operating nut	Repair or replace
Availability of operating wrench	Make sure wrench is available
Cracked or peeled paint, exposed rust unpainted metal	Remove rust, paint hydrant as necessary
Identification and notification of an impaired hydrant — clause a
The owner or owner's designee shall notify the fire department in writing, not less than 48 hours prior to the impairment, of a preplanned impairment of a private fire hydrant.
Identification and notification of an impaired hydrant — clause b

The owner or the owner's designee shall orally notify the fire department immediately of an emergency impairment of a private fire hydrant. The owner of owner's designee shall provide written notice of the emergency impairment to the fire department as soon as practicable.
Identification and notification of an impaired hydrant — clause c

The owner or owner's designee shall affix an impairment tag to an impaired hydrant at the commencement of a preplanned impairment and at the time of discovery of an emergency impairment. Impairment tags are available from the fire department.
Identification and notification of an impaired hydrant — clause d

Once the necessary inspection and testing confirm that repairs have restored a private fire hydrant to operational status, the owner or the owner's designee shall remove the impairment tag and shall notify the fire department that the hydrant is operational.

Records shall indicate the procedure performed concerning the inspection, testing, maintenance, correction, and repair of a private hydrant. Such records shall include the organization that performed the work, the results, and the date, as well as such other pertinent information as the fire department shall require.
Records shall be maintained by the owner or the owner's designee.

The owner or owner's designee shall submit to the fire chief of the fire department a record of the annual inspection, and any records of any testing, maintenance, corrections and repairs of each private fire hydrant and its components. Such records shall be provided to the fire chief of the fire department no more than five business days after the completion of any inspection
The owner shall retain the original records of a private fire hydrant for the life of the private fire hydrant.
All records other than those referred to in subsection (d), above, shall be retained for a period of one year after the next inspection, test, maintenance, correction or required by this article.
A civil penalty of not more than $500.00 may be imposed for a violation of the sections of this article. Each day that the violation continues shall constitute a separate violation of this article.

In addition to the enforcement procedures available, the Village of Stickney may pursue any remedy authorized by law, including, but not limited to, declaratory and injunctive relief. In any action or proceeding for a purpose mentioned in this section, the Circuit Court of Cook County, or any court with jurisdiction of such action or proceeding has the power to, and in its discretion may, issue a restraining order or a preliminary injunction, as well as a permanent injunction, upon such terms and under such conditions as will do justice and enforce the purposes set forth above.

Except as otherwise provided in section 18-359 below, no property owner within the village shall construct. maintain or modify, or cause to be constructed, maintained or modified, any building, structure, or addition, in a manner which fails to support adequate radio coverage within said building, structure, or addition for the village's public safety services, including, but not limited to, emergency management, police, fire and public works services. For purposes of this article, "modify" shall mean substantial changes to, or the addition of, exterior and interior walls using a material that could impact radio coverage, such as brick, cinder block or concrete, or any other structural alteration or change that could impact radio coverage. A certificate of occupancy shall not be issued for any building or structure which fails to comply with this requirement.

The frequency range which must be supported shall be 150 through 160 MHzFD, 450 through 480 MHzPD, 746 through 776 MHz. and 794 through 806 MHz or as otherwise established and required in writing by the village as being necessary for public safety purposes.

For purposes of this article, adequate radio coverage shall be defined as a minimum signal level of DAQ3 (delivered audio quality 3) available in 95 percent of the area as agreed to be in the coverage acceptance test plan by the village and the radio system manufacturer prior to system testing.
All radio coverage systems and components shall comply with all applicable federal regulations including but not limited to FCC 47 CFR Part 90.219.
Radio amplification system allowed — clause a

In the event a radio amplification system is necessary to provide adequate coverage, buildings and structures may be equipped with any of the following:

(1)

A radiating cable system;

(2)

An internal multiple antenna system with FCC type accepted bidirectional VHF and UHF amplifiers as needed to encompass the frequency range stated in subsection 18-350(b) above or frequency range subsequently established by the village; or

(3)

A system that has been approved by the village as being capable of providing amplification to meet the requirements of this article.
Radio amplification system allowed — clause b

The radio amplification system shall be capable of operating at 100 percent capacity on an independent battery and/or generator system for a period of at least 12 hours without external power input. The battery system shall automatically charge in the presence of external power input. There shall be no connection between the radio amplification system and the fire alarm system.
All signal booster components shall be contained in a National Electrical Manufacturer's Association (NEMA) 4-type waterproof cabinet.
Battery systems used for the emergency power source shall be contained in a NEMA 3R or higher-rated cabinet.
Equipment shall have FCC or other radio licensing authority certification and be suitable for public safety use prior to installation.
Where a donor antenna exists, isolation shall be maintained between the donor antenna and all inside antennas to not less than 20dB greater than the system gain under all operating conditions.
Bi-directional amplifiers (BDAs) used in emergency responder radio coverage systems shall have oscillation prevention circuitry.

The installation of amplification systems or systems that operate on or provide the means to cause interference on any emergency responder radio coverage shall be coordinated and approved by a village fire code official.
Loss of normal AC power supply.
Low batter capacity at 70 percent reduction of operating capacity.
The communications link between the fire alarm system and the emergency responder radio enhancement system.
Additional frequencies and change of frequencies

The emergency responder radio coverage system shall be capable of modification or expansion in the event frequency changes are required by the FCC or other radio licensing authority, or additional frequencies are made available by the FCC or other radio licensing authority.

The building owner shall modify or expand the emergency responder radio coverage system at his or her own expense in the event frequency changes are required by the FCC or other radio licensing authority, or additional frequencies are made available by the FCC or other radio licensing authority. Prior approval of a public safety radio coverage system on previous frequencies does not exempt the building from this section.

The fire code official shall have the authority to require "as built" design documents and specifications for emergency responder communications coverage systems. The documents shall be in a format acceptable to the fire code official.

Acceptance testing for an in-building or in-structure radio amplification system is required, upon completion of the installation of the radio amplification system. It is the property owner's responsibility to have the radio amplification system tested to ensure that two-way coverage on each floor of the building is a minimum of DAQ3.

Each floor of the building or structure shall be divided into a grid of approximately 40 equal areas. A maximum of two nonadjacent areas will be allowed to fail the test. In the event that three of the areas fail the test, in order to be more statistically accurate, the floor may be divided into 80 equal areas. In such event, a maximum of four nonadjacent areas will be allowed to fail the test. If the radio amplification system continues to fail the test after eight testing attempts, the property owner shall repair, replace, alter or upgrade the radio amplification system to meet the DAQ3 coverage requirement. Talk back testing from the site to the village's E911 communications center shall use a four-watt UHF portable transceiver with public safety speaker/microphone and flexible antenna attached, and a five-watt VHF transceiver with speaker/microphone and flexible antenna. A spot located approximately in the center of a grid area will be selected for the test, then the radio will be keyed to verify two-way communication to and from the outside of the building or structure. Once the spot has been selected, use of another spot within the grid area will not be permitted. Field strength testing instruments are to be recently calibrated (within the past 12 months) and of the frequency selective type incorporating a flexible antenna similar to the ones used on the hand-held transceivers.

The gain values of all amplifiers shall be measured, and the results kept on file with the property owner so that the measurements can be verified each year during the annual tests. In the event that the measurements results become lost, the property owner will be required to rerun the acceptance test to reestablish the gain values.

When an in-building or structure radio amplification system is installed, the property owner shall, at the owner's sole cost and expense, test all active components of the radio amplification system including, but not limited to, the amplifier, the power supplies and the back-up batteries, a minimum of once every 12 months. Amplifiers shall be tested to ensure that the gain is the same as it was upon initial installation and acceptance of the radio amplification system. Back-up batteries and power supplies shall be tested under load for a period of one hour to verify that they will operate during an actual power outage. All other active components shall be checked to determine that they are operating within the manufacturer's specification for the intended purpose.

In addition to the annual test as referred to in section 18-353 above, the property owner shall, at the owner's sole cost and expense, perform a radio coverage test at least once every five years to ensure that the radio amplification system continues to meet the requirements of this chapter. The acceptance test procedures, set forth above in section 18-352 shall apply to such tests.
Village personnel shall have the right to enter into the property at any reasonable time to conduct field testing to verify the required level of coverage.

Where other nonpublic safety amplification systems installed in buildings reduce the performance or cause interference with the emergency responder communications system, the nonpublic safety amplification system shall be corrected or removed.

When a building or structure fails to support adequate radio coverage, the owner of same must present a compliance plan to the village's fire chief within 90 days after the discovery of said failure to address the inadequate radio coverage. The property owner shall, within one year of the approval of the compliance plan, have the approved plan enacted. A one-year extension for the implementation of the compliance plan may be granted by the fire chief with an approved phase in plan.

All tests under sections 18-353 and 18-354 of this article shall be conducted, documented and signed by a person in possession of a current FCC general radio telephone operator license. All test records shall be retained at the inspected premises by the property owner, with a copy thereof being submitted to the village's fire chief within 30 days of when the test has been conducted. In the event of the test indicates a failure to comply with the requirements this chapter, appropriate repairs shall be made, and additional tests conducted until said tests indicate that the building or structure meets the requirements of this chapter.

Village personnel, or their agents, after providing reasonable notice to the owner or his/her/their/its representative, shall have the right to enter any building or structure which is subject to the requirements of this chapter to conduct field­ testing to be certain that the required level of radio coverage is present.

The property owner shall be responsible for making any repairs, replacements or upgrades to the radio amplification system, as directed by the village, should the radio amplification system fail to work properly. Once a radio amplification system has been found to be in compliance with the requirements of this article, the property owner shall be responsible for maintaining said radio amplification system. For each radio amplification system, a copy of the contract shall be provided to the fire chief, or their designee, with the name of the contractor who will supply a 24 hours per day, seven days per week emergency response within two hours after notification by either the village or the property owner. The maintenance contract shall contain contact information relative to the contractor including, but not limited to, working phone numbers. The property owner shall also submit contact information for the property owner to the village, including, but not limited to, phone numbers for the property owner and his/her/their/its representative, if any.
Single-family residences, regardless of when constructed or modified; or
Buildings where the construction or modifications occurred prior to January 1, 2022.

A building permit shall be required for the installation of any radio amplification system. The fee for the permit shall be the minimum permit fee as established by the building permit fee schedule set forth in section 18-103 of this Code.

Failure to comply with, or a violation of any of the requirements of this article, shall subject the violator to a fine of not to exceed $750.00, with each day a violation continues constituting a separate and distinct offense. In addition to the fine, a violation of any of the requirements of this article shall be grounds for the village to revoke any previously issued certificate of occupancy for the building or structure.

903.4.2.2. Occupant notification. All sprinklered buildings shall be provided with occupant notification appliances.
IFC change: Accessible and identified sprinkler test valves

903.4.2.3. Access to test valves. Fire sprinkling system inspectors test valves shall be accessible at all times and located no more than six (6) feet above the finished floor. On multiple riser systems test valves shall be marked as to which riser and area it tests.

903.4.3. Floor Control Valves is hereby revised to read:

903.4.3. Floor Control Valves. Approved supervised indicating control valves shall be provided at the point of connection to the riser on each floor in multiple story buildings. Provide floor control valves with water flow switches for each floor.
IFC change: Locating an alarm in a sprinklered building

903.4.4. Automatic Sprinklers. Where automatic sprinklers provide protection to an area with an approved flow switch interconnected to the fire alarm system, and the area is easily identifiable as to the location of the activation, additional automatic detectors are not required. When a building has numerous rooms protected by a zoned sprinkler system, additional smoke detectors shall be required to provide a more rapid means to identify the location of a fire.
IFC change: Sprinkler hydraulic safety-factor review
903.3.5.3. Minimum Safety Factor. Provide a minimum 10% or 5 psi minimum safety factor, and the system demand shall be 5 psi minimum above the season low water flow test supply.
IFC change: Hydraulic nameplate information on drawings

IFC change: Outside fire-pump test header
903.9. Fire Pump Test Header. Provide an outside test header on fire pump installations.
IFC change: Private hydrant spacing and FDC proximity

903.10. Private Fire Hydrants. Fire hydrants shall be provided around the perimeter of the building in 300 feet increments. A fire hydrant shall be located within 100 feet of the fire department connection on the fire protection water supply to the building. Fire flow requirements are subject to the provisions of Appendix B.
IFC change: Outdoor access to riser and pump rooms
903.11. Outdoor Access. Provide an outdoor access to the sprinkler riser valve room and fire pump room.
IFC change: Sprinkler valve-room fire separation

IFC change: Warehouse hose-valve coverage and supply

903.13. Warehouse Storage Areas. In all storage areas exceeding 20,000 square feet and in all storage areas exceeding 12 feet in height, provide inside 2 ½ inch fire hose valves with 1 ½ inch reducer to a 1 ½ inch connection. Locate the valve at each door entrance to the warehouse and/or storage area. Provide additional 2 ½ inch fire hose valves so that no portion of the warehouse and/or storage area is more than 120 feet maximum travel distance to a fire hose valve. Show the locations of all obstructions and/or racks on the drawing.

The fire hose valves system pipings shall be:

1.

A separate riser piping system.

2.

The 2 ½ inch valves shall be supplied by a minimum of 4 inch with 2 ½ inch drops to each valve.

3.

Where system pressures exceed 100 psi, provide reduced pressure field adjustable type valves.

IFC change: Multi-tenant retail alarm and entrance strobe

907.2.24. Unsprinkled Buildings and Structures. An approved automatic alarm system shall be installed in all use groups not provided with an automatic sprinkler system. Automatic smoke detection shall be used except where ambient conditions would result in nuisance alarm conditions.

The building and environmental inspector shall cause to be inspected all existing buildings or structures where specific information exists that a building or structure is in an unsafe condition so as to endanger life, health, or safety of the occupant of the structure, occupants of the neighboring structures, or the general public.
Enforcement and investigation procedures—Buildings, houses and condominiums — clause 1

Proper and legal use and/or uses conforming to those regulations for the zoning district in which the building or structure is located and the applicable provisions of the Zoning Code of the Village of Stickney.
Enforcement and investigation procedures—Buildings, houses and condominiums — clause 2
Illegal construction work not done under a village permit.
Enforcement and investigation procedures—Buildings, houses and condominiums — clause 3

Conditions that exist in a building or structure, causing an unsafe condition so as to endanger life, health, or safety of the occupant of the structure, occupants of the neighboring structures, or the general public.
Enforcement and investigation procedures—Buildings, houses and condominiums — clause 4
Improper or illegal additions or alterations to any structure or property as defined by the Zoning Code of the Village of Stickney.
Enforcement and investigation procedures—Buildings, houses and condominiums — clause 5
Establishment of apartment units in basements or attics of structures located in single family residential districts.
Certificate of inspection—Buildings, houses and condominiums

A certificate of inspection shall be issued only if the building or structure meets all requirements of the building and zoning code as related to items stated in section 18-64 and any other items required for compliance with the zoning code. It shall be illegal for any person, agent, broker partnership, beneficiary, corporation, firm or company to sell, change or otherwise transfer ownership in any way of any building, house or condominium unit without first obtaining a certificate of inspection. When such inspection shall disclose violations of zoning provision, building code or fire regulations, the building and environmental inspector shall notify, in writing, the owner, agent, occupant of the measures necessary to bring the property into a safe condition within 15 days of the service of such notice unless an extension is granted by the building and environmental inspector.

The building and environmental inspector shall take action on any application for permit no later than the third working day after said application is made (Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays excepted). It shall be illegal for any one to sell, change, or transfer ownership in any way of any building or structure in the Village of Stickney without first obtaining a certificate of inspection and occupancy.
Denial of permit, certificate of inspection or certificate of occupancy

No permit, certificate of inspection or certificate of occupancy shall be issued for any dwelling, apartment or any other place of residence that is not in compliance with the building and zoning codes of the Village of Stickney or is not fit or safe for human habitation. The building and environmental inspector shall determine whether a dwelling, apartment or other place of residence is in compliance with the building and zoning codes of the Village of Stickney or if it is unfit or unsafe for human habitation, if the building and environmental inspector finds that conditions exist which are dangerous or injurious to the health, welfare or safety of the occupant or occupants thereof, or the occupants of neighboring dwellings, apartments or other structures, or to residents of the municipality. Such conditions include, without being limited to, defects increasing the hazard of fire, accident or other calamities; lack of adequate ventilation, light or sanitary facilities; dilapidation, disrepair, or structural defect; uncleanliness or vermin infestation, or any other condition as determined by the building and environmental inspector.

In the event of a denial of any permit, certificate of inspection or certificate of occupancy, a conditional permit or certificate may be issued by the building and environmental inspector permitting conveyance or occupancy upon the express condition that the work necessary to cure the violation(s) in the inspection report is performed during a certain period of time, as specified by the building and environmental inspector.

No permit shall issue to the owner of any dwelling, apartment or any other place of residence if said owner has any local ordinance violation tickets that remain unpaid or has a debt that is in arrears owed to the village as of the time of application for the permit.
Removal of waste material and debris

It shall be the duty of any person repairing, remodeling, or erecting any building or structure in the village to remove all waste matter and debris from the site within two weeks after completion of the work.
Elevator, passenger and freight, escalators, handicapped lifts, dumb waiters and dock lifts safety, inspections and permits — clause a

Certain documents shall be kept on file at the office of the village clerk, be marked and designated as the National Electrical Code (316 NEC 1999), an International Codes and Standards Organization and the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME A17, 2001 Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators), together with all supplements thereto, is hereby adopted as the elevator safety code of the village for the control of elevators, dumb waiters, escalators, lifts, moving walks and dock lifts as herein provided; and each and all of the regulations and provisions except for any penalty provisions of said documents, are hereby referred to, adopted, and made a part hereof, as if fully set out in this section.
Elevator, passenger and freight, escalators, handicapped lifts, dumb waiters and dock lifts safety, inspections and permits — clause b

No new elevator, escalator, dumb waiter, dock lift, or residential lift shall be installed within the village without first obtaining a permit for such installation. The office of the village clerk is hereby authorized to, together with his duly appointed assistants, to issue permits for the installation of all new elevators, escalators, lifts, dock lifts, and dumb waiters. If they conform with the requirements of the aforesaid documents adopted by reference by the village herein. The fee required to be paid for the permit for the installation of any such elevator, escalator, lift, dumb waiter and dock lift shall be $120.00.
Elevator, passenger and freight, escalators, handicapped lifts, dumb waiters and dock lifts safety, inspections and permits — clause c

No elevator, escalator, lift, dumb waiter or dock lift shall be altered, repaired or replaced without first obtaining a permit from the village. The office of the village clerk is hereby authorized, together with his duly appointed assistants, to issue permits for alterations, repairs and replacements to any elevator, escalator, lift, dumb waiter and dock lift found to be in conformance with the requirements of the documents adopted by reference herein.
Elevator, passenger and freight, escalators, handicapped lifts, dumb waiters and dock lifts safety, inspections and permits — clause d
Elevator, passenger and freight, escalators, handicapped lifts, dumb waiters and dock lifts safety, inspections and permits — clause e

Any person violating, resisting or opposing the enforcement of any of the provisions of this section, or lawful order of the office of the village clerk, or his duly appointed assistants, shall, upon conviction, be punished as provided for in this Code. Any builder or contractor who shall construct any building in violation of the provisions of this section, and any architect who shall design, draw plans for, or have supervision of such building, or shall permit to be constructed in violation of the provisions, or shall the violator refuse to obey an order of the provisions herein, shall upon conviction, be punished as provided in this Code.
Boarding up of windows, door or building — clause a

Except as provided in this section, no person shall cause or allow any window of any building in the village to be boarded up or covered with any opaque material, including but not limited to wood, pressed board or other opaque materials, not ordinarily used for windows. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any window which is broken may be temporarily covered with any such opaque material for a period not to exceed 30 days.
Boarding up of windows, door or building — clause b

It shall be unlawful for any person owning, leasing or controlling any building upon any plot of ground within the corporate limits of the village to allow the windows and doors of such building to fall into a state of disrepair and remain open to the elements. This includes, but is not limited to, missing or broken windows and missing or broken doors.
